newsitem.title: JAPAN: LDP tells union hard to meet request for tax cut.
newsitem.headline: LDP tells union hard to meet request for tax cut.

text.p: The top policy-maker of Japan's ruling party responded to a request by executives of Japan's largest labour group by saying it would be extremely difficult to cut taxes by two trillion yen in 1997 due to fiscal constraints, a union official said.

The labour group, Rengo, called for tax cuts in a meeting with Liberal Democratic Party officials in order to reduce financial burdens of wage earners resulting partly from an increase in Japan's sales tax and to achieve sustainable economic growth, the official said.
The Rengo official quoted the LDP's Taku Yamasaki as saying it was difficult to create new revenue to finance the tax cuts demanded as the government was carrying out fiscal reforms.
"Given current fiscal conditions, it is extremely difficult to cut taxes by two trillion yen in 1997," Yamasaki was quoted as saying.
